audit.whatIsWrong: The chart hands Graves levels 1 through 4-5 while whys[2] and whys[3] say the lane tips to you the moment Miasma is up, and the page is graded 7/10 difficulty on a matchup the packet scores 53.15% across 333 games — the largest sample in this slice.
audit.why: A 53% lane over 333 games is not a 7/10. The prose read — his levels, then yours from 3 — is the honest one, and the difficulty grade was the part out of step.
audit.corrected: diffRating moved to 6/10 with the difficulty line and final rating updated to match. Chart cells left alone; the level 3 and 4-5 cells still contradict their own whys and are flagged for the user.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw is called the green light on five lines with no number, and dosFull[0] tells you to burst him 'after the charges are spent' — Quickdraw has no charges.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s and Riot's text adds 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill', so counting seconds is wrong: count his autos. Smoke Screen is 26s at rank 1, End of the Line 13s and Collateral Damage 100s.
audit.corrected: Charge language removed, real numbers written in, and the auto-attack cooldown reduction stated so you time the dash by his attacks instead of a stopwatch.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most usable interaction in the matchup is absent from both layers: nothing says his shotgun cannot shoot through minions.
audit.why: Riot's New Destiny text: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.' Standing with a minion between you and Graves means his entire basic-attack pattern — the thing that also shortens his Quickdraw — physically stops. Separately End of the Line 'detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain', so hugging a wall detonates it on you early.
audit.corrected: Minion-block written into the level 1-2 spike, the early text, whys[0], the wants list and the key-interactions slot; the wall-detonation caveat added to the late text.

edits.before: This is where the treadmill takes over. Ranks in Q and E let you chain near-free Twin Fangs — refunded off Q or W poison — on anything your DoT touches, while his shotgun has to reload its two shells between bursts. Hold W for the moment he Quickdraws in to shotgun you: grounding the dash mid-animation traps him in the cloud, and your leveling move speed lets you sidestep his second shell. At 6, Petrifying Gaze flips his all-in — when he commits the dive, stun him face-on and shred him in the refund-chain before his armor-stacked Quickdraw build can tank it.
edits.after: This is where the treadmill takes over. Ranks in Q and E let you chain near-free Twin Fangs — refunded off Q or W poison — on anything your DoT touches, while his shotgun reloads between bursts. Hold W for the moment he Quickdraws in: grounding traps him in the cloud, and every auto he lands shortens that 16s dash, so watch his attacks rather than a stopwatch. Keep a minion in the bullet line whenever you can. At 6, Petrifying Gaze flips his all-in — when he commits the dive, stun him face-on and shred him in the refund-chain before his armour lead can tank it.

edits.before: You stay ahead here as long as you didn't feed his early kills into a tanky lead. Your single-target Twin Fang DPS out-grinds his burst-and-reset pattern, and W still hard-counters his one repositioning tool — a grounded Graves with Quickdraw on cooldown is a stationary target for poison and Twin Fang. Watch his roams and jungle skirmishes since he's a mobile skirmisher who leaves lane; ward his dash paths, and in any straight 1v1 keep him poisoned and grounded so he can never kite out of your range.
edits.after: You stay ahead here as long as you didn't feed his early kills into a tanky lead. Your single-target Twin Fang DPS out-grinds his burst-and-reset pattern, and W still hard-counters his one repositioning tool — a grounded Graves with Quickdraw down is a stationary target. Do not retreat along a wall: End of the Line collides with terrain and detonates early, so a hugged wall turns his poke into a full hit. Ward his dash paths, keep a minion in his bullet line, and in any straight 1v1 keep him poisoned and grounded so he never kites out.
